$comment: LANE-O (closes verdict 2 of [[D-CONFIG-NO-DESCRIPTOR-FOR-SETLOCALE-FMODE-ENVIRON]]): the pe64 RUN witness for `_fmode` and `_environ` reached THE WAY THE SDK REACHES THEM -- by `#include <stdlib.h>`, through pe-gated MACROS onto the `__p__fmode` / `__p__environ` accessors, with NO `extern` declaration anywhere in the source. ** WHY A MACRO AND NOT A DATA ROW, WHICH THE REGISTRY ROW ALREADY RULED PERMANENT: MEASURED 2026-08-10 on TWO CONCURRING INSTRUMENTS (GNU objdump 2.42 `-p`, whose bracketed index is 0-BASED, and MSVC dumpbin 14.44.35207 `-exports`, which prints real ORDINALS) over ALL 2,484 exports of the live C:/Windows/System32/ucrtbase.dll 10.0.26100.8875: `_fmode` and `_environ` are BOTH ABSENT, while `__p__fmode` is ORDINAL 88 (RVA 0x00099570) and `__p__environ` ORDINAL 87 (RVA 0x00093370). msvcrt.dll (1,330 exports) is the mirror image -- `_fmode` ordinal 306 and `_environ` ordinal 270 ARE data exports there and NEITHER accessor exists -- so the CRT migration is exactly what made the data-row answer impossible. Under [[D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT]] a `kind: object` row for either name would break the LOAD (0xC0000139) of every binary that touched it; for pe this class is ACCESSOR-OR-NOTHING. * THE SDK AGREES RATHER THAN MERELY PERMITTING, which is what makes the macro the FAITHFUL realization and not a workaround: ucrt/stdlib.h:255 is literally `#define _fmode (*__p__fmode ())` and :1171 `#define _environ (*__p__environ())`, each the DEFAULT arm (the direct `extern int _fmode;` at :250 is the opt-in, behind `_CRT_DECLARE_GLOBAL_VARIABLES_DIRECTLY`). ! ONE WIDELY-MISREAD DETAIL, corrected because it was mis-stated once: `_environ`'s poison spelling at :1168 (`#define _environ crt_usage_error__do_not_reference_global_pointer_directly__environ`) is NOT the default -- it sits under `#ifndef _CRT_V12_LEGACY_FUNCTIONALITY`, and :1163-1165 DEFINES that macro whenever `_CRT_BEST_PRACTICES_USAGE` is absent, which it is by default. The conclusion (UCRT never offers data access) is unchanged; the REASON is. * WHY `__p__fmode` AND NOT the `_get_fmode`/`_set_fmode` pair the registry row floated: `(*__p__fmode())` is an LVALUE, so `_fmode = _O_TEXT;` keeps working exactly as on MSVC, whereas a getter/setter pair cannot be assigned through and would have silently changed the surface from an object to a function call. `_get_fmode` ships anyway (ordinal 320, MEASURED) but ONLY as this witness's INDEPENDENT ORACLE; `_set_fmode` (ordinal 1777) is deliberately not shipped -- no consumer, no over-ship. ** EVERY LAYER IS AN AGREEMENT AGAINST AN INDEPENDENT ORACLE, NEVER A MAGIC VALUE, and that is the deliberate improvement over the predecessor witness, which pinned `_fmode == 0` -- a CRT-version fact that read IDENTICALLY to a dead binding, i.e. a layer that could pass for the wrong reason. exit 2 = `_get_fmode` itself failed (guards the oracle BEFORE anything trusts it); exit 3 = the macro and UCRT's own getter DISAGREE about the same state (a macro expanding to a wrong accessor, or an accessor bound to the wrong export); exit 4 = the store through the lvalue did not land; exit 5/6 = after the store the getter cannot see the new value (the two paths are not the same state); exit 7 = restore failed; exit 8 = `_environ` handed back nothing; exit 9/10 = an entry is not NAME=VALUE with a non-empty NAME (a binding one indirection off fails the '=' scan on garbage rather than appearing to pass); exit 11 = an empty vector; exit 12/13 = entry[0] malformed or its name over-long; exit 14 = getenv cannot see a variable `_environ` claims exists; exit 15 = getenv and `_environ` DISAGREE on the value (a stale table); exit 16/17 = stdout write/flush failed, which also proves the CRT's own stdio still works after `_fmode` was poked and restored. THE ENVIRONMENT'S CONTENT IS NEVER ASSERTED (it is host-dependent) -- only its STRUCTURE plus the getenv agreement, the shipped_environ pattern -- so the stdout pin is host-independent. It is pinned with CRLF because this is a pe64-only manifest and the UCRT translates the newline in text mode (the shipped_atexit precedent). RED-ON-DISABLE: drop stdlib.json's pe `_fmode` macro variant -> `_fmode` becomes an ordinary undeclared identifier and the TU fails to compile, honest and loud; repoint either macro at a wrong accessor (`__p___argv`, say) -> exit 3 or 8; un-ship `__p__fmode` / `__p__environ` -> honest K_SymbolUndefined at link (src/link/linker.cpp:174); un-ship `_get_fmode` -> the ORACLE disappears and the TU fails to compile rather than silently losing a layer. pe64-ONLY, deliberately: these are Microsoft spellings with no glibc or libSystem export, which is also why both symbol rows and both macro variants are gated (`availableObjectFormats: [pe]` / `when.format: pe`) -- declaring them elsewhere would plant undefined imports. The POSIX `environ` spelling is a DIFFERENT row (unistd.json, elf-only, bound GOT-INDIRECT onto the strong `__environ` -- it used to be a copy relocation, which claimed one name of glibc's environ/_environ/__environ alias set and SPLIT the object: D-LK-ELF-COPY-RELOC-CLAIMS-ONE-NAME-OF-AN-ALIAS-SET) witnessed by shipped_environ plus environ_alias_object_identity, and it cannot host a pe arm at all because there is no <unistd.h> on Windows. extern_data_import_pe is the extern-DATA sibling and explains why NEITHER of these names can play that role. The optimized arms prove the accessor call + deref survive the release pipelines.
